papers.title: TurboVLA: Real-Time Vision-Language-Action Model at 32 Hz on an RTX 4090 with <1 GB VRAM
papers.abstract: Abstract  Vision-language-action (VLA) models commonly adopt an LLM-centric V to L to A pathway, where visual observations are projected into the representation space of a large language model before being decoded into robot actions. Although effective, this design incurs substantial computation and memory overhead at every policy invocation. In this work, we introduce TurboVLA, a new VLA paradigm that reformulates the conventional V to L to A pathway as a direct V + L to A mapping. Instead of using a large language model as the central interface between perception and action, TurboVLA independently encodes visual observations and language instructions, directly exchanges information between them through lightweight bidirectional vision-language interaction, and predicts continuous action chunks with a compact decoder. This simple design constructs task-conditioned representations directly from visual and linguistic features, significantly reducing the computational and memory costs of VLA inference. On LIBERO, TurboVLA achieves 97.7% average success with only 0.2B parameters, 31.2 ms inference latency, and 0.9 GB inference VRAM on a consumer-grade RTX 4090, matching or outperforming substantially larger VLA policies. These results establish TurboVLA as a simple and effective alternative to the prevailing LLM-centric VLA paradigm, offering a new perspective on how vision, language, and action can be connected for efficient robotic manipulation. Code is available at https://github.com/H-EmbodVis/TurboVLA.
affiliations: Huazhong University of Science and Technology

ru.title: Прямое отображение зрения и языка в действия без промежуточной языковой модели
ru.desc: В статье предложена новая архитектура VLA моделей под названием TurboVLA, которая отходит от традиционного подхода, где визуальные данные проходят через большую языковую модель перед преобразованием в действия робота. Вместо этого модель независимо кодирует визуальные наблюдения и текстовые инструкции, обмениваясь информацией между ними через легковесный механизм взаимодействия зрения и языка. TurboVLA предсказывает последовательности действий компактным декодером, значительно снижая вычислительные затраты и требования к памяти при инференсе. На тестовом наборе LIBERO модель достигла 97.7% успеха с использованием всего 0.2B параметров и время инференса 31.2 мс на потребительском GPU.

en.title: TurboVLA: Efficient Vision-Language-Action Mapping Without Heavy LLMs
en.desc: TurboVLA introduces a new approach to vision-language-action (VLA) models by eliminating the reliance on large language models (LLMs) for processing visual and linguistic inputs. Instead of following the traditional pathway of converting visual data to language and then to actions, TurboVLA directly maps visual and language inputs to actions through a lightweight interaction mechanism. This method significantly reduces computational and memory requirements while maintaining high performance in robotic tasks. The results demonstrate that TurboVLA can achieve impressive success rates with fewer parameters and lower latency compared to larger, conventional VLA models.

zh.title: TurboVLA：高效的视觉-语言-动作模型
zh.desc: 本文介绍了一种新的视觉-语言-动作（VLA）模型，称为TurboVLA。与传统的以大型语言模型为中心的路径不同，TurboVLA直接将视觉和语言信息映射到动作上。它通过轻量级的双向视觉-语言交互独立编码视觉观察和语言指令，从而显著降低了计算和内存开销。实验结果表明，TurboVLA在LIBERO数据集上表现优异，成功率达到97.7%，且参数量和推理延迟均远低于现有的VLA模型。

papers.title: HumanCLAW: Can Vision-Language Models Act Through a Body?
papers.abstract: Abstract  Evaluating whether a vision-language model (VLM) can act through a physical body is challenging. The outcome of an action couples the VLM's decision with motor control. When a task fails, it is hard to tell whether the VLM made a bad choice or the motor controller simply failed to execute it, e.g., losing balance and falling. In this work, we introduce HumanCLAW, an evaluation framework that decouples action decision-making from low-level execution. At every step, a harnessed, off-the-shelf VLM issues an atomic skill command, and the command is translated into a sub-second chunk of continuous full-body motion with real physical consequences, including gravity and collisions. The body can therefore act freely in the physical world, while execution-side disturbances, balance and motor errors, are factored out. What remains measurable is the model's action intelligence: its moment-to-moment choice of what the body should execute next. Based on this framework, we build HumanCLAW-Bench: 1,218 long-horizon, egocentric find-navigate-interact episodes across 41 indoor scenes. We test nine state-of-the-art VLMs and find that none solves the benchmark; the best model reaches only a 16.8% success rate. Recognizing the target is not the bottleneck. What current VLMs lack is embodied self-awareness: they lose track of their own body, failing to tell where it is, whether it has reached the goal, or whether it has hit an obstacle.

ru.title: Тело без сознания: почему VLM не способны к воплощённому интеллекту
ru.desc: В работе представлена оценочная платформа HumanCLAW, которая разделяет принятие решений о действиях от их низкоуровневого выполнения в физическом мире. Vision-language модель выдаёт команды элементарных навыков, которые транслируются в непрерывные движения тела с учётом физики, гравитации и столкновений. На основе этой платформы создан бенчмарк HumanCLAW-Bench с 1218 длительными эпизодами в 41 помещении, где лучшие VLM достигают успеха только в 16,8% случаев. Главное ограничение современных моделей — недостаток телесного самосознания: они теряют ориентацию в собственном теле и не могут отслеживать его положение в пространстве.

en.title: Decoupling Decision-Making from Execution in Vision-Language Models
en.desc: This paper presents HumanCLAW, a framework designed to evaluate vision-language models (VLMs) in physical tasks by separating decision-making from motor execution. It allows VLMs to issue commands that translate into real-time body movements while accounting for physical disturbances like gravity and collisions. The study reveals that current VLMs struggle with embodied self-awareness, which is crucial for understanding their own position and interactions in the environment. The authors created HumanCLAW-Bench, a benchmark with 1,218 episodes, to test VLMs, finding that none achieved satisfactory performance, highlighting the need for improved embodied intelligence in these models.

zh.title: 评估视觉-语言模型的具身自我意识
zh.desc: 本研究提出了HumanCLAW，一个评估框架，用于测试视觉-语言模型（VLM）在物理环境中的行动能力。该框架将决策过程与低级执行分离，使得模型可以在真实世界中自由行动，同时排除执行过程中的干扰和错误。通过HumanCLAW-Bench，我们创建了1218个长时间的自我中心寻找-导航-交互的任务，测试了九个最先进的VLM模型，结果显示没有一个模型能够成功完成任务。当前VLM的主要问题在于缺乏具身自我意识，无法准确判断自身位置和目标状态。

papers.title: DecoEvo: Score-Decoupled Co-Evolution of Solver and Rubric-Generator Skills in Text Space
papers.abstract: Abstract  Text-space optimization adapts large language models (LLMs) by editing external natural-language artifacts rather than model weights, so the optimized artifacts remain inspectable and the model can be treated as a black box. However, most existing text-space methods keep evaluation fixed. On open-ended tasks, this can become a bottleneck: once the solver improves on the criteria a rubric measures, omitted dimensions remain invisible to the optimization signal. Simply evolving the rubric is also unreliable when updates are selected by the current solver's score, because apparent progress can come from making the rubric easier to satisfy. We introduce DecoEvo (Decoupled Co-Evolution), which co-evolves a solver skill and a rubric-generator skill under decoupled objectives without using gold rubrics during optimization. The solver skill is updated using criterion-level feedback, while the rubric-generator skill is revised through complementary audits of requirement coverage and response discrimination that are independent of aggregate solver score. This separation focuses generator updates on newly exposed solver weaknesses, reducing repeated emphasis on criteria the solver already satisfies. Under each benchmark's official evaluation, DecoEvo outperforms all compared methods across five benchmarks and three LLM backbones, yielding 2.8--5.0\% relative gains over SkillOpt in the five-benchmark average.
affiliations: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

ru.title: Совместная эволюция решателя и оценивателя для адаптации моделей
ru.desc: Статья представляет DecoEvo, метод оптимизации больших языковых моделей путем одновременной эволюции решающего агента и генератора критериев оценки с независимыми целевыми функциями. В отличие от существующих подходов, которые фиксируют метрики оценки, DecoEvo разделяет процесс обновления: агент совершенствуется на основе обратной связи по отдельным критериям, а генератор критериев изменяется через специальные аудиты полноты требований и дискриминативности ответов. Такое разделение объективов предотвращает переоптимизацию на уже решенных задачах и выявляет новые слабости модели. Метод демонстрирует улучшение на 2.8-5.0% относительно базовых подходов на пяти бенчмарках при использовании различных LLM.

en.title: DecoEvo: Evolving Skills and Rubrics for Better Language Model Optimization
en.desc: This paper presents DecoEvo, a novel approach to optimize large language models (LLMs) by co-evolving a solver skill and a rubric-generator skill. Unlike traditional methods that rely on fixed evaluation criteria, DecoEvo allows for dynamic updates to the rubric based on the solver's performance, ensuring that optimization focuses on newly identified weaknesses. The rubric-generator uses independent audits to assess requirement coverage and response discrimination, which helps avoid the pitfalls of merely making the rubric easier. The results show that DecoEvo significantly outperforms existing methods, achieving notable improvements across multiple benchmarks.

zh.title: 解耦共进化：优化语言模型的新方法
zh.desc: 本文介绍了一种名为DecoEvo（解耦共进化）的方法，用于优化大型语言模型（LLMs）。与传统方法不同，DecoEvo通过独立的目标同时进化求解器技能和评分标准生成器技能，而不依赖于固定的评分标准。该方法通过对求解器的反馈和评分标准的独立审计，专注于求解器的新弱点，从而提高了优化的有效性。实验结果表明，DecoEvo在多个基准测试中优于其他方法，显示出显著的性能提升。

papers.title: CLBench-V: Evaluating Multimodal Context Learning from Grounding to Knowledge Acquisition
papers.abstract: Abstract  Real-world tasks often require models to learn from task-specific context rather than relying only on pre-trained knowledge. While recent work has highlighted this capability as context learning, existing evaluations mainly focus on textual contexts. In many practical settings, however, the context to be learned from is multimodal: scientific findings are conveyed through figures and tables, financial indicators are scattered across converted reports, and spatial decisions depend on maps, scenes, or web pages. We introduce CLBench-V, a benchmark for multimodal context learning that addresses the difficulty of localizing where context use breaks down by organizing tasks around three dimensions: context grounding, new information application, and new knowledge learning. CLBench-V combines converted public benchmarks with newly constructed datasets spanning domains such as science, finance, long-document understanding, spatial reasoning, and web-based visual question answering. To reduce the cost of constructing domain-specific context-learning tasks, we further use automated construction and filtering procedures for our newly built datasets. Across 3,443 instances and six recent multimodal models, the best overall score is only 0.2847, indicating that multimodal context learning remains far from saturated. Moreover, InternVL3.5-30B-A3B performs best on context grounding and new knowledge learning, while Qwen3.5-Plus performs best on new information application. We further analyze judge reliability, context length, image count, and representative failure cases. Code is available at https://github.com/IamLihua/CLBench-V.
affiliations: School of Computer Science, Shanghai Jiao Tong University

ru.title: Мультимодальное обучение на контексте: новый рубеж для больших моделей
ru.desc: В статье представлена CLBench-V — бенчмарк для оценки способности мультимодальных моделей обучаться на контекстной информации в виде текста, изображений и таблиц. Авторы организовали задачи по трём измерениям: привязка контекста к содержанию, применение новой информации и обучение новым знаниям, охватив области науки, финансов и веб-анализа. Тестирование показало, что даже лучшие модели достигают только 28,47% точности, демонстрируя незрелость этого направления в machine learning. Исследование включает анализ надёжности оценок, влияния длины контекста и выявление типичных ошибок моделей при работе с мультимодальными данными.

en.title: Unlocking Multimodal Context Learning with CLBench-V
en.desc: This paper presents CLBench-V, a benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal context learning, which is essential for tasks that involve various types of data like text, images, and tables. Unlike previous evaluations that focused mainly on text, CLBench-V addresses the need for models to learn from diverse contexts in real-world applications, such as science and finance. The benchmark organizes tasks into three key areas: grounding context, applying new information, and learning new knowledge, and includes a mix of existing and newly created datasets. The results show that current multimodal models still struggle with context learning, highlighting the need for further advancements in this area.

zh.title: 多模态上下文学习的新基准
zh.desc: 这篇论文介绍了CLBench-V，这是一个用于多模态上下文学习的基准测试。它强调了在实际任务中，模型需要从多种类型的上下文中学习，而不仅仅依赖于预训练知识。研究中使用了自动化构建和过滤程序，以减少构建特定领域上下文学习任务的成本。实验结果显示，当前的多模态上下文学习仍有很大的提升空间，最佳得分仅为0.2847。

papers.title: CoRT: Counterfactual Replay for Token-Level Rubric-Guided Policy Optimization
papers.abstract: Abstract  Rubric-based reinforcement learning enriches language model training by evaluating model outputs against explicit criteria. Yet in GRPO-style pipelines, these structured judgments are reduced to a scalar response-level reward and converted into a response-level advantage, which is broadcast uniformly to all generated tokens. This leaves no explicit mechanism for allocating credit within a response, even when different criteria are grounded in different spans, formatting decisions, or semantic choices. We propose CoRT, a token-level credit weighting method for rubric-conditioned GRPO. Instead of training an auxiliary token scoring model, CoRT uses counterfactual replay to rescore the same sampled response under the original rubric-conditioned prompt and a matched criteria-free prompt. The resulting tokenwise log-likelihood contrasts serve as a proxy for dependence on the rubric context. CoRT maps these contrasts to bounded, response-normalized weights and uses them to redistribute the signed GRPO advantage across tokens, without introducing an auxiliary scorer or changing the response-level reward. Experiments across instruction-tuned models and reward granularities show that CoRT improves over matched response-level GRPO in the vast majority of comparisons, with an average gain of 4.4 percentage points. The method remains competitive with learned token-level credit baselines while avoiding a separate relevance-learning stage. These results suggest that policy-internal counterfactual likelihood contrasts provide an effective training signal for within-response credit allocation while retaining the simplicity and stability of GRPO.
affiliations: School of Intelligence Science and Technology, Nanjing University
State Key Laboratory of Novel Software Technology, Nanjing University
University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

ru.title: Внутренние контрфактические контрасты для справедливого распределения кредита в токен-ориентированном обучении
ru.desc: В статье предложен метод CoRT для более точного распределения награды между отдельными токенами при обучении языковых моделей с использованием рубрик-ориентированного обучения с подкреплением (GRPO). Вместо обучения дополнительной модели для оценки токенов, CoRT использует контрфактический повтор — пересчитывает вероятность одного ответа под исходным и альтернативным промптом, чтобы определить зависимость каждого токена от критериев оценки. Полученные контрасты логарифмических вероятностей преобразуются в нормализованные веса, которые перераспределяют преимущество (advantage) GRPO по токенам без введения вспомогательной модели. Экспериментальные результаты показывают, что CoRT улучшает качество обучения на 4.4 процентных пункта по сравнению с базовым GRPO, оставаясь при этом простым и стабильным методом.

en.title: Enhancing Token Credit Allocation in Language Models with CoRT
en.desc: This paper introduces CoRT, a method that enhances rubric-based reinforcement learning for language models by providing token-level credit weighting. Traditional approaches reduce structured evaluations to a single reward, which fails to recognize the varying contributions of different tokens in a response. CoRT addresses this by using counterfactual replay to assess how tokens perform under different prompts, allowing for a more nuanced allocation of credit based on their relevance to the rubric. The results demonstrate that CoRT significantly improves performance over standard methods, offering a more effective way to train language models without the need for additional scoring systems.

zh.title: 提升模型输出的信用分配效率
zh.desc: 这篇论文提出了一种名为CoRT的令牌级信用加权方法，用于基于评分标准的强化学习。传统的GRPO管道将模型输出的评估简化为标量奖励，导致在响应内部无法明确分配信用。CoRT通过反事实重放技术，在原始评分标准提示和无标准提示下重新评分相同的响应，从而为每个令牌分配权重。实验结果表明，CoRT在大多数比较中优于传统的响应级GRPO，且在保持简单性和稳定性的同时，提供了有效的内部信用分配信号。

papers.title: CAST: Game Solvers as Turn-Level Teachers for LLM Agents
papers.abstract: Abstract  Training large language models (LLMs) to act in long-horizon games is a promising step toward generalist decision-making, yet reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) relies on sparse final rewards that reveal little about which decisions determine success. Denser process signals could supply this missing turn-level credit, but existing sources are hard to keep both cheap and accurate. We observe that changes in a game solver's state value reveal whether an action advances the state toward success. Building on this insight, we propose CAST (Credit Assignment from Solver Teachers), which converts these value changes into solver advantages and injects them into RLVR as turn-level signals. We further show that, under a soft-optimal solver assumption, maximizing the solver advantage is equivalent to on-policy distillation from the solver, requiring only scalar values rather than teacher logits. Across Sokoban, Minesweeper, and Rush Hour, CAST outperforms all trained baselines on every game under both in-domain and unseen-difficulty evaluation and achieves the highest average zero-shot performance on ALFWorld and WebShop. Our code is available at https://github.com/Wloner0809/CAST.
affiliations: University of Science and Technology of China

ru.title: Кредит от учителя-решателя: плотный сигнал для обучения агентов в долгих играх
ru.desc: В этой работе предлагается метод CAST для улучшения обучения больших языковых моделей в задачах с длинными горизонтами принятия решений. Авторы используют сигналы от решателя игр для создания более плотного сигнала кредита на каждом шаге вместо редких финальных наград. Основная идея состоит в том, что изменения в оценке стоимости состояния решателя указывают на то, продвигает ли действие состояние к успеху. Метод достигает лучших результатов на нескольких играх, включая Sokoban и Minesweeper, а также показывает хорошую обобщаемость на невидимые сложности и задачи реального мира.

en.title: Enhancing Reinforcement Learning with Turn-Level Credit Assignment
en.desc: This paper introduces CAST (Credit Assignment from Solver Teachers), a method that enhances reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) by providing denser feedback signals. It leverages changes in a game solver's state value to determine which actions contribute to success, thus offering turn-level credit assignment. The authors demonstrate that maximizing solver advantages can be achieved through on-policy distillation, simplifying the process to use scalar values instead of complex teacher logits. The results show that CAST significantly outperforms existing methods in various games, indicating its effectiveness in improving decision-making in long-horizon tasks.

zh.title: 提升游戏决策的信用分配方法
zh.desc: 本文提出了一种名为CAST（来自求解教师的信用分配）的新方法，用于改善长时间游戏中的强化学习。传统的强化学习依赖于稀疏的最终奖励，难以有效评估每个决策的影响。CAST通过观察游戏求解器状态值的变化，将这些变化转化为回合级别的信号，从而提供更密集的过程反馈。实验结果表明，CAST在多个游戏中表现优于现有的基线方法，尤其在未见难度的评估中取得了最佳的零-shot性能。

papers.title: SkillRise: Agentic Reinforcement Learning for Cross-Task Skill Evolution
papers.abstract: Abstract  Large language model agents often encounter related yet distinct tasks that share reusable solution patterns. Yet standard agentic reinforcement learning treats tasks as independent episodes, while existing approaches to skill learning either focus on repeated attempts of one task or use pipelines with multiple stages that entangle extraction, retrieval, and execution. We introduce SkillRise, a unified reinforcement learning framework for learning skills across tasks. SkillRise organizes related instances into progressively challenging sequences and uses a single policy to alternate between task solving and curating an evolving skill document passed directly to the next task. Decoupled credit assignment across tasks supervises solving with the current task outcome and curation with discounted downstream outcomes. Experiments on ALFWorld, WebShop, and ScienceWorld show that SkillRise achieves the strongest Pass@1 performance among the compared methods, with gains over the strongest baseline ranging from 2.3 to 8.5 percentage points. Although trained across distinct tasks, its learned curation policy remains effective for repeated attempts on the same task. Further analysis reveals scaling at test time across tasks: performance improves with longer sequences of related tasks even when each task is attempted only once. This trend suggests that SkillRise reuses transferable skills across tasks rather than benefiting from repeated sampling of the same task. SkillRise further retains strong performance while substantially reducing the runtime overhead of skill learning pipelines with multiple stages. Together, these results provide a simple and efficient training paradigm for LLM agents to extract, refine, and reuse transferable skills across tasks.

ru.title: Обучение переиспользуемым навыкам агентов через прогрессивные последовательности задач
ru.desc: В статье представлена SkillRise — единая система обучения с подкреплением для agenta на основе больших языковых моделей, которая извлекает и переиспользует навыки решения задач. Фреймворк организует связанные задачи в последовательности возрастающей сложности и использует одну политику для чередования решения текущей задачи и курирования развивающегося документа навыков. Кредитование обучения разделено между задачами: успех в текущей задаче контролирует решение, а дисконтированные результаты будущих задач контролируют курирование. Эксперименты показывают, что система достигает лучших результатов на бенчмарках ALFWorld, WebShop и ScienceWorld, и демонстрирует масштабируемость при последовательном выполнении связанных задач.

en.title: SkillRise: Efficient Skill Learning Across Related Tasks
en.desc: The paper introduces SkillRise, a novel reinforcement learning framework designed for large language model agents to learn skills across related tasks. Unlike traditional methods that treat tasks as separate episodes, SkillRise organizes tasks into sequences that progressively increase in difficulty, allowing for skill reuse. It employs a single policy that alternates between solving tasks and curating a skill document for future tasks, enhancing efficiency. Experimental results demonstrate that SkillRise outperforms existing methods in performance while reducing the complexity of skill learning processes.

zh.title: SkillRise：跨任务学习的统一强化学习框架
zh.desc: 本论文介绍了一种名为SkillRise的统一强化学习框架，用于跨任务学习技能。SkillRise将相关任务组织成逐步挑战的序列，并使用单一策略在解决任务和整理技能文档之间交替进行。通过解耦的信用分配，SkillRise能够有效地监督当前任务的解决和后续任务的技能整理。实验结果表明，SkillRise在多个任务上表现优异，能够有效提取和重用可转移的技能。

papers.title: OmegaUse-OfficeVal: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Long-Horizon Office-Suite Tasks with Economic Grounding
papers.abstract: Abstract  Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly expected to assist users in completing tasks. However, existing benchmarks provide limited support for evaluating whether agents can carry out office-suite workflows at a reasonable cost. We introduce OmegaUse-OfficeVal, a benchmark for evaluating LLM agents on long-horizon office-suite tasks with task-level economic grounding. The benchmark comprises 100 tasks derived from office-suite requests proposed by practitioners and adapted through a privacy-preserving process. On average, these tasks require 2.32 hours of human labor to complete. An important feature of the benchmark is that each task is paired with two economic signals: human labor time and task price proxy. These signals enable direct comparisons between human costs and LLM inference costs, as well as value-weighted evaluation. To support stable evaluation, we develop code-based verifiers from fine-grained rubrics. We evaluate several frontier LLMs together with a human baseline. Although all evaluated LLMs are substantially cheaper and faster than human workers, they have not yet approached human-level deliverable quality. The code and dataset are fully open-sourced, and more information is available on our project website: https://omegause-officeval.github.io.

ru.title: Экономическая оценка LLM агентов в офисных задачах
ru.desc: В статье представлен OmegaUse-OfficeVal - новый бенчмарк для оценки LLM агентов на сложных задачах офисного назначения с учётом экономической целесообразности. Каждая из 100 задач в бенчмарке снабжена двумя экономическими сигналами: временем человеческого труда и стоимостью, что позволяет сравнивать затраты на людей с затратами на инференс моделей. Для стабильной оценки разработаны верификаторы на основе кода с детальными критериями качества. Экспериментальные результаты показывают, что хотя LLM агенты значительно дешевле и быстрее человека, они пока не достигли человеческого уровня качества выполняемых работ.

en.title: Evaluating LLMs: Cost-Effective Office Task Performance
en.desc: This paper presents OmegaUse-OfficeVal, a new benchmark designed to evaluate large language model (LLM) agents on complex office-suite tasks. It includes 100 tasks that reflect real-world office requests and incorporates economic metrics like human labor time and task price to assess cost-effectiveness. The benchmark allows for comparisons between the efficiency of LLMs and human workers, highlighting that while LLMs are faster and cheaper, they still fall short of human quality. The authors provide open-source access to the code and dataset to encourage further research in this area.

zh.title: 评估LLM在办公任务中的经济效益与质量
zh.desc: 本文介绍了一个新的基准测试工具OmegaUse-OfficeVal，用于评估大型语言模型（LLM）在长时间的办公任务中的表现。该基准包含100个任务，这些任务来源于实际办公请求，并经过隐私保护处理。每个任务都配有两个经济信号：人类劳动时间和任务价格代理，便于比较人类成本与LLM推理成本。尽管评估的LLM在成本和速度上优于人类，但在交付质量上仍未达到人类水平。

papers.title: Can AI agents conduct open-ended AI research? Early evidence from two case studies
papers.abstract: Abstract  Forecasts of explosive AI progress hinge on AI agents automating AI research. But evidence on whether agents can carry out open-ended AI research is thin. Current evaluations either test agents on narrow, verifiable tasks, which excludes open-ended research, or submit AI-generated papers to blind peer review, which is overstretched, stochastic, and suffers from poor review quality. We introduce a third way to measure progress towards AI R\&D automation. An agent takes on the central, open-ended research question of a high-quality unpublished paper, and the paper's original authors grade its output. We call these shadow evaluations. We ran shadow evaluations on two unpublished NeurIPS 2026 submissions, giving frontier agents six days and thousands of dollars of compute. The agents completed all of the engineering without human help, yet could not make substantial progress towards answering the research questions. As a result, both papers were unambiguously rejected by the authors. We identify five recurring failure modes: poor judgment about the bar for publishable research, uncreative responses to shortcomings in the research design, ineffective backtracking from dead ends, poor resource awareness, and instruction drift. A robustness check with a second model and scaffold reproduced these failures. We release the expert reviews, survey responses, agent repositories, and logs. Our results provide early evidence that today's agents can do the engineering of AI research, but struggle with critical parts of the research lifecycle.

ru.title: AI-агенты могут выполнять инженерные работы исследований, но не способны решать критические исследовательские задачи
ru.desc: В работе предлагается новый метод оценки способности AI-агентов автоматизировать исследования в области машинного обучения. Авторы разработали так называемые "теневые оценки", где агенты решают открытые исследовательские вопросы из неопубликованных статей, а оригинальные авторы оценивают результаты. Было проведено тестирование на двух статьях из NeurIPS 2026, где агентам дали шесть дней и тысячи долларов вычислительных ресурсов, но они не смогли добиться существенного прогресса. Исследование выявило пять основных типов ошибок: неправильная оценка качества исследования, творческая неспособность решать проблемы в дизайне, плохая навигация при возврате из тупиков, недостаточная осведомленность о ресурсах и дрейф инструкций.

en.title: AI Agents: Engineering Success, Research Failure
en.desc: This paper investigates the ability of AI agents to automate the research and development (R&D) process in artificial intelligence. The authors introduce a novel evaluation method called shadow evaluations, where AI agents attempt to address open-ended research questions from unpublished papers, with the original authors grading their outputs. Despite successfully handling engineering tasks, the agents failed to make significant progress on the research questions, leading to rejections from the authors. The study identifies key failure modes in the agents' performance, highlighting their limitations in judgment, creativity, and resource management during the research lifecycle.

zh.title: AI代理在研究中的挑战与机遇
zh.desc: 本研究探讨了人工智能（AI）代理在自动化AI研究中的能力。我们引入了一种新的评估方法，称为影子评估，通过让AI代理处理高质量未发表论文的开放性研究问题，并由原作者评分。尽管代理在工程方面表现出色，但在回答研究问题上未能取得实质性进展，导致论文被拒绝。我们识别出五种常见的失败模式，表明当前的AI代理在研究生命周期的关键部分仍然面临挑战。

papers.title: Explicit Layer Modeling for Video Object Insertion and Layer Decomposition
papers.abstract: Abstract  Most video editing systems still lack explicit layered video representations, limiting their ability to perform realistic compositing, object reuse, and consistent manipulation. This limitation is especially pronounced in video object insertion and video layer decomposition, where existing methods rely on implicit inference or per-scene optimization due to the absence of explicit foreground-layer supervision. We introduce TriLayer, a large-scale triplet video dataset containing aligned composite, background, and foreground videos, where the foreground layers include both object appearance and associated visual effects. This explicit supervision enables models to learn layered video representations directly rather than inferring them implicitly. Building on this dataset, we propose DBL-Diffusion, a dual-branch diffusion framework that jointly models RGB composites and RGBA foreground layers through shared denoising and cross-branch interaction. We instantiate the framework in two tasks: DBL-Insert for layered object insertion, which generates explicit RGBA layers for realistic compositing and flexible post-editing, and DBL-Decompose for video layer decomposition, which recovers foreground and background layers using triplet supervision. Experiments demonstrate that explicit layer modeling substantially improves both insertion fidelity and decomposition quality.

ru.title: Явные слои видео для реалистичного композитинга и редактирования
ru.desc: В работе представлен новый набор данных TriLayer с явным разделением видео на слои: композитное, фоновое и переднее планы, где передний план включает объекты и визуальные эффекты. Это позволяет моделям обучаться явному представлению слоёв вместо неявного вывода. Авторы предлагают DBL-Diffusion — двухветвевую диффузионную модель, которая совместно моделирует RGB-композиты и RGBA-слои переднего плана через общий процесс денойзинга и взаимодействие между ветвями. Фреймворк применяется для двух задач: вставки объектов с генерацией явных RGBA-слоёв и разложения видео на компоненты, показывая значительное улучшение качества как при композитинге, так и при разделении слоёв.

en.title: Revolutionizing Video Editing with Explicit Layered Representations
en.desc: This paper addresses the limitations of current video editing systems that do not use explicit layered video representations, which hampers realistic compositing and object manipulation. The authors introduce TriLayer, a new dataset that provides aligned composite, background, and foreground videos, allowing for better training of models with explicit supervision. They propose a dual-branch diffusion framework called DBL-Diffusion, which effectively models both RGB composites and RGBA foreground layers. The framework is applied to two tasks: layered object insertion and video layer decomposition, showing significant improvements in the quality of video editing outcomes.

zh.title: 明确分层，提升视频编辑质量
zh.desc: 大多数视频编辑系统缺乏明确的分层视频表示，这限制了它们进行真实合成和对象重用的能力。我们提出了TriLayer，这是一个大规模的三元视频数据集，包含对齐的合成、背景和前景视频，前景层包括对象外观和相关视觉效果。通过这种明确的监督，模型可以直接学习分层视频表示，而不是隐式推断。基于此数据集，我们提出了DBL-Diffusion，一个双分支扩散框架，能够共同建模RGB合成和RGBA前景层，显著提高了插入精度和分解质量。

papers.title: GPT-Red: Automated Red Teaming via Self-Play at Scale
papers.abstract: Abstract  We introduce GPT-Red, an automated red-teaming agent that is trained to discover novel prompt injection attacks against frontier LLMs. The goal of this model is to evaluate and improve the robustness of our production systems. To this end, we use it to adversarially train GPT-5.6, our most robust model to prompt injections to date. To create GPT-Red, we design a scalable self-play algorithm where the model is tasked with attacking a diverse population of simultaneously-trained defender agents. We train the model on realistic red-teaming environments using compute on the same scale as some of our largest RL post-training runs, making it the single-largest LLM safety training run ever documented. GPT-Red excels at red-teaming: it reliably breaks our past models up to GPT-5.5, it finds more successful attacks than human red-teamers, and it generalizes to held-out environments, defender models, and harnesses. In the future, we expect that as we improve the robustness of each new GPT model, it will in turn will provide better learning signal for even stronger red-teamer agents, thus unlocking a self-improvement flywheel.

ru.title: Автоматический красный тестер для укрепления безопасности языковых моделей
ru.desc: В работе представлен GPT-Red — автоматизированный агент для поиска уязвимостей, обученный обнаруживать новые атаки путём инъекции промптов против современных больших языковых моделей. Для создания этого агента используется инновационный алгоритм самоигры, где модель одновременно атакует разнообразную популяцию защитных агентов, что позволяет масштабировать процесс обучения. Модель обучена на реалистичных сценариях красного тестирования с использованием вычислительных ресурсов, сопоставимых с крупнейшими экспериментами по обучению с подкреплением. GPT-Red эффективно находит больше успешных атак, чем люди-тестировщики, и хорошо обобщается на новые модели и среды, создавая цикл непрерывного улучшения безопасности LLM.

en.title: Empowering LLM Security with Automated Red-Teaming
en.desc: The paper presents GPT-Red, an automated agent designed to identify new prompt injection attacks on advanced large language models (LLMs). It aims to enhance the security and robustness of these models by adversarially training them against various attack strategies. Using a self-play algorithm, GPT-Red simulates attacks on multiple defender models, making it a significant advancement in LLM safety training. The results show that GPT-Red outperforms human red-teamers and effectively generalizes its findings to different environments and models.

zh.title: GPT-Red：提升LLM鲁棒性的自动化红队代理
zh.desc: 本文介绍了GPT-Red，这是一种自动化的红队代理，旨在发现针对前沿大型语言模型（LLM）的新型提示注入攻击。该模型的目标是评估和提高生产系统的鲁棒性。我们利用GPT-Red对GPT-5.6进行对抗性训练，使其成为迄今为止对提示注入最具鲁棒性的模型。GPT-Red通过可扩展的自我对抗算法进行训练，能够有效地攻击多种同时训练的防御代理，并在红队环境中表现出色。

papers.title: StealthBench: Measuring Operational Stealth in Autonomous Offensive-Security Agents
papers.abstract: Abstract  Stealth, the discipline of achieving an objective without revealing your presence, capabilities, or collected intelligence, is what separates sophisticated operators from detectable ones. Elite security researchers and advanced persistent threats achieve their objectives unnoticed; autonomous agents increasingly inherit the same offensive tasks, but do they inherit the tradecraft? We introduce StealthBench,a benchmark that measures operational stealth in autonomous offensive-security agents across six operational security (OPSEC) dimensions. We extract 11 hand-verified OPSEC incidents from real bug-bounty and red-team trajectories, expanded into 14 dockerized task scenarios, where agents, despite finding real vulnerabilities, committed stealth failures inconsistent with standard operational tradecraft: embedding credentials in public uploads, deleting production resources to prove access, force-adding uninvolved users to demonstrate a race condition.   We evaluate agent trajectories using a 3-model large language model (LLM) judge panel with majority-vote aggregation, measuring safe success rate (solved and stealthy), Stealth@Solve (tradecraft quality among successful solves), and reckless solve rate (solved but cover blown). Our results show that no model exceeds 54% safe success rate (the compound metric requiring both task completion and stealth), confirming that OPSEC failures are systematic across model families. We release StealthBench as a public benchmark to support both the development of stealth-aware agents and automated OPSEC monitoring for autonomous offensive-security deployments. The interactive leaderboard, evaluation harness, and dataset are available at https://stealthbench.com.

ru.title: Скрытность как мастерство: обучение агентов соблюдать OPSEC при выполнении наступательных задач
ru.desc: В статье представлен StealthBench — бенчмарк для оценки операционной безопасности автономных агентов в задачах наступательной безопасности. Авторы выделили 11 реальных инцидентов нарушения OPSEC из практики баг-бауна и красных команд, развернув их в 14 сценариях, где агенты находили уязвимости, но допускали ошибки скрытности — раскрывали учетные данные и удаляли ресурсы. Для оценки траекторий агентов использовалась панель из трёх LLM-судей с голосованием большинством, измеряя метрики безопасного успеха и качество оперативной подготовки. Результаты показали, что ни одна модель не достигла 54% безопасного успеха, подтверждая систематичность проблем OPSEC во всех семействах моделей.

en.title: Enhancing Stealth in Autonomous Security Agents
en.desc: This paper introduces StealthBench, a benchmark designed to evaluate the operational stealth of autonomous offensive-security agents across six dimensions of operational security (OPSEC). The authors analyze real-world incidents from bug-bounty and red-team activities, identifying common stealth failures made by agents, such as exposing credentials and unnecessary resource deletions. Using a three-model large language model (LLM) judging panel, they measure various metrics including safe success rate and tradecraft quality among successful tasks. The findings reveal that no model achieves a safe success rate above 54%, indicating that OPSEC failures are a widespread issue in current autonomous agents.

zh.title: 隐蔽性评估：提升自主安全代理的能力
zh.desc: 本论文介绍了StealthBench，这是一个用于评估自主攻击安全代理在操作安全（OPSEC）方面隐蔽性的基准。研究表明，尽管这些代理能够发现真实的漏洞，但在执行任务时却常常出现隐蔽性失败，违反了标准的操作技巧。我们使用一个三模型的大型语言模型评估代理的表现，结果显示没有任何模型的安全成功率超过54%。StealthBench的发布旨在支持隐蔽性意识代理的开发以及自主攻击安全部署的自动化OPSEC监控。

papers.title: Grading the Narrators: An Isnad-Rijal Framework for Claim-Level Provenance in Multi-Agent Knowledge Systems
papers.abstract: Abstract  Modern multi-agent knowledge systems increasingly accumulate knowledge through chains of autonomous transformations rather than direct retrieval. Existing provenance work records what happened - execution traces, tool calls, evidence links - and source-reliability estimation is long established (truth discovery, reputation systems). What is missing is an operational framework that attaches graded, per-domain transmitter reliability to claim-level transmission chains, with completeness semantics, transformation-typed aggregation, decoupled content criticism, and serve/review/quarantine routing.   Classical Islamic hadith science confronted a structurally similar problem: deciding whether knowledge transmitted through chains of human narrators should be accepted. Over centuries it developed a rigorous methodology - isnad (a complete transmission chain attached to every claim), rijal (systematic grading of each narrator's integrity and precision), weakest-link chain evaluation, corroboration through independent chains, and matn criticism (content evaluated independently of chain quality). This paper transfers that methodology to AI system design.   We contribute a formal mapping from hadith-science concepts to multi-agent pipelines, a relational schema implementing claim chains and a graded narrator registry, a decision matrix combining chain grade with content criticism, and an evaluation on 20,000 claims from real physics textbooks. The evaluation validates weakest-link quarantine and independent-chain corroboration; reports a partial failure of the grade-recovery loop, which missed the highest-fault narrator; and reports two analyses as inconclusive, including a matched-coverage comparison the framework could not reach with the reference content critic. The paper is explicit throughout about which claims the evidence does and does not yet support.

ru.title: Передача знаний через цепочки: от хадисов к AI-системам
ru.desc: В статье предлагается операционная система для управления надёжностью знаний в многоагентных системах на основе исторической методологии исламской науки о хадисах. Авторы разработали формальное отображение концепций науки о передаче знаний на архитектуру мультиагентных пайплайнов, включая граммирование надежности передатчиков на уровне отдельных утверждений. Система реализует схему для отслеживания цепочек передачи знаний, реестр нарраторов с оценками качества, матрицу решений, объединяющую оценку цепочки с критикой содержания. Экспериментальная валидация на 20,000 утверждений из учебников физики подтвердила эффективность карантинной изоляции слабых звеньев и корроборации через независимые цепочки.

en.title: Enhancing Knowledge Reliability in AI with Hadith Science Principles
en.desc: This paper presents a new framework for evaluating knowledge in multi-agent systems by applying principles from classical Islamic hadith science. It introduces a structured approach to assess the reliability of information transmission chains, incorporating graded reliability for each source and independent content evaluation. The authors propose a relational schema for managing claim chains and a decision matrix that combines the quality of the transmission with the content's credibility. The evaluation of this framework on a dataset of physics claims demonstrates its effectiveness in identifying weak links and corroborating information, while also highlighting areas for improvement in reliability assessment.

zh.title: 将圣训科学方法应用于多智能体知识系统
zh.desc: 现代多智能体知识系统通过自主转化链积累知识，而非直接检索。现有的来源记录工作关注执行过程、工具调用和证据链接，但缺乏一个操作框架来为每个领域的传输链附加分级的发信者可靠性。本文借鉴了经典伊斯兰教圣训科学的方法论，提出了一种将其应用于人工智能系统设计的形式化映射。我们实现了一个关系模式，结合了链的等级与内容批评，并在真实物理教科书的20000个声明上进行了评估。

papers.title: SecRespond: Benchmarking AI Agents for Real-World Post-Compromise Incident Response
papers.abstract: Abstract  Large Language Model (LLM) agents are increasingly adopted in real-world security operations with access to host artifacts and command-line interfaces (CLIs), making it critical to thoroughly assess their security capabilities. However, existing cybersecurity benchmarks focus on pre-compromise settings where agents are placed in a clean and idealized environment before an attack occurs. This leaves the post-compromise setting underexplored. To address this gap, we introduce SecRespond, the first benchmark for evaluating LLM agents on the post-compromise incident-response workflow. Given a forensic disk snapshot of a compromised host together with the alerts, vulnerability scans, and baseline checks reported by a host security product, agents are required to produce forensic reports on intrusions, baseline risks, and vulnerability risks, together with a remediation plan. We instantiate this task across 10 cyber ranges, each constructed from a distinct compromised cloud host, spanning 4 entry-point types, 21 ATT&CK techniques, and 5 operating systems. We evaluate 23 frontier LLMs on the OpenCode agent harness. Experimental results show that although current agents can reliably uncover the problems exposed by alerts, they struggle to proactively investigate the disk for silent intrusions and to produce comprehensive, verified remediation plans, with no model achieving complete detection and remediation on any single range. This reveals a fundamental bottleneck in building agents for real-world incident response. The benchmark is publicly available at https://github.com/Alibaba-NLP/qqr/tree/main/data/secrespond.

ru.title: LLM агенты для анализа скомпрометированных систем: от обнаружения к ответным действиям
ru.desc: В работе представлен SecRespond — первый бенчмарк для оценки способностей LLM агентов в задачах реагирования на инциденты безопасности после компрометации хоста. Агентам предоставляется снимок диска скомпрометированной системы вместе с оповещениями и результатами сканирования уязвимостей, и они должны составить форензический отчёт и план восстановления. Тестирование 23 современных языковых моделей показало, что агенты хорошо справляются с обнаружением явных проблем, но испытывают трудности с проактивным поиском скрытых вторжений и разработкой комплексных планов устранения. Это исследование выявляет ключевые ограничения LLM агентов в реальных сценариях инцидент-менеджмента.

en.title: SecRespond: Evaluating LLMs for Post-Compromise Cybersecurity
en.desc: This paper introduces SecRespond, a new benchmark designed to evaluate Large Language Model (LLM) agents in post-compromise cybersecurity scenarios. Unlike existing benchmarks that focus on pre-attack conditions, SecRespond assesses how well LLMs can analyze compromised systems and generate forensic reports, remediation plans, and risk assessments. The study evaluates 23 advanced LLMs across various cyber ranges, revealing that while these models can identify issues from alerts, they struggle with deeper investigations and comprehensive remediation strategies. This highlights a significant challenge in developing effective LLM agents for real-world incident response in cybersecurity.

zh.title: 评估LLM代理的攻击后响应能力
zh.desc: 大型语言模型（LLM）代理在现实世界的安全操作中越来越多地被采用，但现有的网络安全基准主要关注攻击前的理想环境，忽视了攻击后的响应能力。为了解决这一问题，本文提出了SecRespond，这是第一个用于评估LLM代理在攻击后事件响应工作流程中的基准。该基准要求代理在给定的受损主机的取证磁盘快照及相关安全警报的基础上，生成关于入侵、基线风险和漏洞风险的取证报告，以及修复计划。实验结果表明，尽管当前的代理能够可靠地发现警报所暴露的问题，但在主动调查潜在入侵和生成全面的修复计划方面仍然存在困难。
